title: The Fox and the Leopard

full_text:
A proud leopard and a clever fox were disputing with each other as to who possessed the greater beauty and nobility. The leopard stood upon a mossy rock, stretching his supple limbs and displaying his golden pelt covered with exquisite dark rosettes.

"Look upon my magnificent coat!" purred the leopard boastfully. "There is not a creature in all the wilderness whose skin can match the elegance, symmetry, and splendor of my spots. I am a living masterpiece of velvet and gold, while your coat is nothing but plain, dusty orange fur!"

The fox listened patiently, cleaning his whiskers with a nimble paw. When the leopard had exhausted his conceited praise, the fox looked up and replied with calm, smiling dignity:

"You have a very handsome skin, friend Leopard, and no one denies the beauty of your spots. But I am far more beautifully endowed than you: for while your beauty is painted merely upon your outside hide, my spots are within—woven into the keenness of my mind, the sharpness of my wit, and the resourcefulness of my spirit. When your skin is worn out, you will have nothing left, but my inner wisdom serves me for all my days!"
moral: A brilliant mind is far more beautiful and valuable than a painted skin.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Fox and the Leopard"?
options: Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?

By running away from every problem

options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
